paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage teaches: when Jesus doesn't move on your schedule, it doesn't mean He doesn't love you. The text says Jesus loved Martha and her sister and Lazarus (John 11:5). Then it says that when He heard Lazarus was sick, He stayed where He was for two days (John 11:6). Love and waiting sit in the same story, and the writer puts them side by side on purpose.

Now, I get it, because waiting is hard. When you're stuck in the dark, two days feels like a whole YEAR. But Jesus told them the sickness was "for the glory of God, so that the Son of God may be glorified through it" (John 11:4), and He said He was glad He wasn't there "so that you may believe" (John 11:15). So the waiting wasn't a mistake, and it wasn't Jesus looking the other way. He had a purpose for it, and it was for His glory and for their faith.

And look at the disciples, friend. They thought He meant a nap, and Thomas figured they were all heading off to die with Him (John 11:13, 16). I think they were doing their best with what they could see. So here's your takeaway, baker: bring Jesus the hard thing, trust that He loves you, and keep walking with Him even when you can't see how it ends. This story isn't over, and I'd say that's good news.
